note: Definitions are written for this tool. Formulas use explicit brackets (BEDMAS) and match the standard definitions cited; where a convention varies between sources, the note says which one the engine uses.

terms.definition: Everything it costs to deliver the project: land, transfer taxes, studies, approvals, levies, construction, soft costs, and construction interest capitalized into the loan.
terms.formula: TDC = Σ(cost lines) + Σ(component costs) + capitalized interest
terms.note: Interest paid in cash after completion is a financing cost, not part of TDC. The analysis buckets include it so every dollar is counted.

terms.definition: Rent and other income actually collected, minus the costs of running the property. Excludes debt payments, income tax and depreciation.
terms.formula: NOI = (potential rent × (1 − vacancy)) + other income − operating expenses

terms.definition: Potential rent after vacancy and credit loss, plus other income. NOI is EGI minus operating expenses.
terms.formula: EGI = (potential rent × (1 − vacancy)) + other income

terms.definition: The income return the finished, stabilized project earns on what it cost to build. The development counterpart of a cap rate.
terms.formula: Yield on cost = stabilized NOI ÷ TDC
terms.note: The engine uses untrended NOI (today's rents), the more conservative convention.

terms.definition: The income return an investor accepts when buying a stabilized property. Dividing NOI by a cap rate gives value.
terms.formula: Cap rate = NOI ÷ market value  ⇔  value = NOI ÷ cap rate

terms.definition: How much more the project yields than the market cap rate for an existing building. It is the reward for taking on construction and lease-up risk.
terms.formula: Development spread = yield on cost − exit cap rate
terms.note: Practitioners often look for 150–200 basis points.

terms.definition: The annual rate at which the project's cash flows break even in present-value terms. Unlevered uses project cash flows before debt; levered uses the investor's equity cash flows.
terms.formula: IRR = r such that Σ(CFₜ ÷ (1 + r)^t) = 0; annual = ((1 + monthly IRR)^12) − 1
terms.note: Solved numerically. Shown as unavailable when cash flows never change sign, no root exists, or more than one rate gives NPV = 0 (then use NPV at a stated discount rate).

terms.definition: All future cash flows discounted back to today at the required return, minus what is spent. Positive means the project beats that required return.
terms.formula: NPV = Σ(CFₜ ÷ (1 + r)^t), t = 0…n; monthly r = ((1 + annual r)^(1/12)) − 1

terms.definition: How many times NOI covers the year's loan payments (interest and principal). Lenders set a minimum.
terms.formula: DSCR = NOI ÷ annual debt service; maximum loan = PV of (NOI ÷ DSCR) over the amortization

terms.definition: The loan as a share of the property's appraised value.
terms.formula: LTV = loan ÷ value

terms.definition: The construction loan as a share of total project cost. Construction lenders cap it; equity funds the rest first.
terms.formula: LTC = loan ÷ TDC; equity required = (1 − LTC) × budget

terms.definition: How many dollars investors get back for each dollar they put in, over the whole hold.
terms.formula: Equity multiple = Σ(equity distributions) ÷ Σ(equity contributions)
terms.note: Gross basis: calls and distributions are summed separately, and at master-plan level one block’s distributions are not assumed to fund another block’s calls.

terms.definition: Profit as a share of total development cost (TDC), with numerator and denominator on the same basis. The headline figure is after capitalized construction interest, over TDC including that interest; the before-financing figure excludes financing from both. Different from margin on revenue: always check the denominator.
terms.formula: Profit on cost = (total revenue − TDC) ÷ TDC, where TDC includes capitalized construction interest
terms.note: Developers commonly look for roughly 15–20% on condo projects; under 5% is generally unviable (Brandon Donnelly).
terms.source: Brandon Donnelly: Demystifying the development pro forma

terms.definition: Land price as a share of the project's expected sales revenue. A quick check on whether the land price fits what the project can sell for.
terms.formula: Land-to-revenue = land price ÷ total revenue
terms.note: GTA high-density buyers paid about 10–15% of expected revenue in 2018–19 (416 higher, 905 lower). Dated benchmark.
terms.source: Bullpen & Batory, GTA High-Rise Land Insights Report Q4-2019

terms.definition: Land price divided by the floor area the site can be built to. Lets you compare sites of different sizes and densities.
terms.formula: Land $/buildable ft² = land price ÷ buildable GFA
terms.note: GTA high-density average $111 in Q4-2019; former City of Toronto $187 for 2019. Dated benchmark.
terms.source: Bullpen & Batory, GTA High-Rise Land Insights Report Q4-2019

terms.definition: The most you could pay for land and still hit your target return, after every other cost and the required profit come out of the project's value.
terms.formula: Residual land value = value − (all non-land costs + target profit), solved iteratively when financing depends on land

terms.definition: The level monthly payment that repays a loan over its amortization.
terms.formula: Payment = (P × r) ÷ (1 − ((1 + r)^−n)); r = annual rate ÷ 12, n = months; P ÷ n when r = 0

terms.definition: All floor area that gets built and paid for, including below-grade parking and mechanical space. Drives hard cost.
terms.formula: GCA = Σ(floor areas, above and below grade)

terms.definition: Floor area as the zoning by-law counts it, with by-law-specific exclusions. Drives FSI and zoning permissions, not cost.
terms.formula: Defined by the applicable zoning by-law

terms.definition: Density: by-law counted floor area divided by lot area. Never computed from construction area.
terms.formula: FSI = by-law GFA ÷ lot area

terms.definition: The area buyers or tenants actually pay for. Smaller than GCA because of corridors, cores, walls and amenity space.
terms.formula: Efficiency = (NSF + NLA) ÷ above-grade GCA

terms.definition: How much of the built floor area is sellable or leasable.
terms.formula: Efficiency = (NSF + NLA) ÷ above-grade GCA

terms.definition: Municipal, regional and education levies per new unit or per m², set by by-law to fund growth infrastructure. Deferrals change when you pay, not how much.
A school-board levy on new residential units, set by the board's by-law.
A charge of up to 4% of land value on buildings of 5+ storeys and 10+ units, where the municipality has a CBC by-law.
Land for parks or a payment instead, capped by site size under the Planning Act.
Ontario tax on property purchases; Toronto adds its own municipal land transfer tax (MLTT).
Ontario's 25% tax on residential purchases by foreign buyers.

terms.term: Harmonized sales tax / input tax credits
terms.definition: 13% in Ontario. Registrants making taxable sales recover HST paid on inputs as input tax credits; new rental triggers self-supply HST at first occupancy.
Money the landlord spends fitting out commercial space for a tenant, and fees paid to brokers who lease it.

terms.term: Environmental site assessment / Record of Site Condition
terms.definition: Phase One reviews history, Phase Two samples soil and groundwater. An RSC is filed with the province before changing to a more sensitive use, such as industrial to residential.
Requires a technical review for work within 60 m of its infrastructure.
Federal housing agency. MLI Select insures rental mortgages with higher leverage and longer amortization in exchange for affordability, accessibility and energy commitments.
How developed a cost estimate is. Class D is concept-level with the widest range; Class A is pre-tender with the narrowest.
terms.source: Alberta Infrastructure, after ASTM E2516-11 and CIQS

terms.definition: From the simulation: 10% of outcomes fall below P10, half below P50, 90% below P90.
Hundredths of a percent: 100 bps = 1%.
The firm that builds the project, either for a fixed price (GC) or by managing trades for a fee (CM).
What the property pays the owner each year after operating costs and loan payments, before income tax.
terms.formula: BTCF = NOI − annual debt service

terms.definition: One year of before-tax cash flow as a share of the equity invested.
terms.formula: Cash-on-cash = BTCF ÷ equity invested

terms.definition: How fast units lease or sell: the share of available units taken up in a period.
terms.formula: Absorption = units leased or sold in period ÷ units available

terms.definition: The annual property tax bill. Ontario taxes the MPAC assessed value at a rate set by class (for example, new multi-residential is taxed at the residential rate in Toronto).
terms.formula: Levy = tax rate × assessed value; assessed value = market value × assessment ratio

terms.definition: A tax rate expressed per thousand dollars of assessment.
terms.formula: 1% = 10 mills

terms.term: Land value capture / tax increment financing
terms.definition: Tools that recover part of the land-value increase created by public investment: development charges, CBCs, special assessments, transfer of development rights. TIF borrows against future property-tax growth in an area; it redirects revenue rather than creating it.
